We utilize the generalized inclusion-exclusion principle (GIE) for the union of $k=7$ sets, $U = \bigcup_{i=1}^7 A_i$:
$$|U| = \sum_{i=1}^7 |A_i| - \sum_{1 \le i < j \le 7} |A_i \cap A_j| + \sum_{1 \le i < j < k \le 7} |A_i \cap A_j \cap A_k| - \dots$$
Due to the assumption that no three subsets intersect, all terms involving three or more intersections are zero.
$$|U| = \sum_{i=1}^7 |A_i| - \sum_{1 \le i < j \le 7} |A_i \cap A_j|$$

To maximize $|U|$, we must maximize the sum of the sizes of the 7 chosen sets and minimize the sum of their pairwise overlaps, subject to the global constraints.

**Analysis of Global Constraints:**
The condition that no three subsets intersect means that any element $x \in X$ can belong to at most two of the 15 subsets.
If an element $x$ belonged to three sets ($A_i, A_j, A_k$), then $x \in A_i \cap A_j \cap A_k$, violating the constraint.
Since the union $|U|$ is a subset of $X$, the absolute maximum size is limited by $|X|=56$.

**Construction for Maximization:**
We aim to construct a set system where $|\bigcup_{i=1}^7 A_i| = 56$. This is achieved if the 7 subsets cover the entire ground set $X$.
We can construct this scenario by first defining $A_1, \dots, A_7$ such that they form a partition of $X$. (For instance, divide $X$ into 7 sets of size 8). In this case, $A_i \cap A_j = \emptyset$ for $i \ne j$.
$$\sum_{i=1}^7 |A_i| = 56 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{i<j} |A_i \cap A_j| = 0$$
Thus, $|\bigcup_{i=1}^7 A_i| = 56$.

We must verify that the remaining 8 sets ($A_8, \dots, A_{15}$) can be defined without violating the triple intersection constraint globally.
Since $A_1, \dots, A_7$ are mutually disjoint, any triple intersection involving two or more of these sets is automatically empty (e.g., $A_1 \cap A_2 \cap A_8 = \emptyset$).
We can define $A_8, \dots, A_{15}$ such that they only overlap with $A_1, \dots, A_7$ pairwise, and overlap with each other pairwise, while ensuring that no element belongs to more than two sets overall. Since the set $X$ has 56 elements, and we only need to accommodate pairwise intersections, this construction is possible.

Because the union size is fundamentally bounded by the size of the universe, $|X|=56$, and we have demonstrated a valid construction where the union achieves this bound, the maximum possible size is 56.
